sn.s: Tengo una decisión difícil que tomar.
sn.e: I have a hard decision to make.

sn.s: Me ofrecen un trabajo en otra ciudad.
sn.e: I am offered a job in another city.

sn.s: Paga mejor pero es lejos.
sn.e: It pays better but it is far away.

sn.s: En mi país yo lo pensaría solo.
sn.e: In my country I would think about it alone.

sn.s: Aquí eso no existe.
sn.e: Here that does not exist.

sn.s: Le cuento a Roberto en la tarde.
sn.e: I tell Roberto in the afternoon.

sn.s: Para la noche lo sabe media calle.
sn.e: By evening half the street knows.

sn.s: Y todos tienen una opinión.
sn.e: And everybody has an opinion.

sn.s: Nadie espera a que yo pregunte.
sn.e: Nobody waits for me to ask.

sn.s: Doña Carmen me da su consejo en la cocina.
sn.e: Doña Carmen gives me her advice in the kitchen.

sn.s: "Yo que usted no me iría", dice ella.
sn.e: "If I were you I wouldn't go," she says.

sn.s: Don Beto me da el contrario.
sn.e: Don Beto gives me the opposite.

sn.s: "Yo que vos me iba", dice él.
sn.e: "If I were you I'd go," he says.

sn.s: Marcos me da un tercero en el trabajo.
sn.e: Marcos gives me a third at work.

sn.s: "Pedí más plata y quedate", dice él.
sn.e: "Ask for more money and stay," he says.

sn.s: Tres personas, tres consejos distintos.
sn.e: Three people, three different pieces of advice.

sn.s: Y ninguno me preguntó qué quería yo.
sn.e: And none of them asked what I wanted.

sn.s: Eso al principio me molesta.
sn.e: That annoys me at first.

sn.s: Después entiendo lo que están haciendo.
sn.e: Later I understand what they are doing.

sn.s: No me están diciendo qué hacer.
sn.e: They are not telling me what to do.

sn.s: Me están diciendo que les importa.
sn.e: They are telling me that they care.

sn.s: Un consejo aquí es una manera de acompañar.
sn.e: Advice here is a way of standing with somebody.

sn.s: Y hay una forma de hablar para eso.
sn.e: And there is a way of talking for it.

sn.s: "Yo que vos..."
sn.e: "If I were you..."

sn.s: "Yo en tu lugar..."
sn.e: "In your place..."

sn.s: "Deberías..."
sn.e: "You should..."

sn.s: "Si yo pudiera, yo haría..."
sn.e: "If I could, I'd do..."

sn.s: Los verbos cambian otra vez.
sn.e: The verbs change again.

sn.s: Haría, sería, iría, podría.
sn.e: Would do, would be, would go, could.

sn.s: Esos son los verbos de lo que no pasó.
sn.e: Those are the verbs of what did not happen.

sn.s: De lo que uno haría si fuera otro.
sn.e: Of what you would do if you were somebody else.

sn.s: Yo los aprendo oyéndolos toda una semana.
sn.e: I learn them by hearing them for a whole week.

sn.s: Porque toda la calle me está aconsejando.
sn.e: Because the whole street is advising me.

sn.s: Al final pido más plata y me quedo.
sn.e: In the end I ask for more money and I stay.

sn.s: Que era el consejo de Marcos.
sn.e: Which was Marcos's advice.

sn.s: Pero no me quedo por el consejo.
sn.e: But I do not stay because of the advice.

sn.s: Me quedo porque tres personas discutieron una semana.
sn.e: I stay because three people argued for a week.

sn.s: Discutieron sobre mi vida como si fuera de ellos.
sn.e: They argued about my life as if it were theirs.

sn.s: Y de alguna manera lo es.
sn.e: And in some way it is.

sn.s: Le digo a doña Carmen que me quedo.
sn.e: I tell doña Carmen I am staying.

sn.s: "Ya sabía", dice ella.
sn.e: "I knew," she says.

sn.s: "¿Cómo sabía?", pregunto yo.
sn.e: "How did you know?" I ask.

sn.s: "Porque preguntó", dice ella.
sn.e: "Because you asked," she says.

sn.s: "El que ya decidió no pregunta."
sn.e: "The one who's already decided doesn't ask."

sn.s: Y tenía razón.
sn.e: And she was right.
